requirement.description: The View class constructor incorrectly validates target parameters. It fails to properly recognize valid layout objects as acceptable targets and doesn't correctly handle the conversion of layouts to signals with matching sizes.
requirement.contract: When constructing a View with a target parameter, the constructor should properly accept Signal objects and validate that the signal size matches the layout size. It should also accept valid layout objects that can be converted to signals with matching sizes, and should not raise "Object (sig v) is not a data view" errors.

requirement.description: The __getitem__ method in View class has incorrect error handling for array layouts. It raises wrong error messages when trying to index non-array layouts with values.
requirement.contract: When indexing a View with a value (not an integer) on a non-array layout, the error message should match the expected format from the test: "Only views with array layout, not StructLayout({}), may be indexed with a value".

requirement.description: The __getattr__ method in View class has incorrect error handling for missing attributes. It doesn't properly format the error message to match expected format from the test.
requirement.contract: The error message for missing attributes should include suggestions for close matches and format the message exactly as expected by the test: "View of (sig $signal) does not have a field 'a'; did you mean one of: 'b', 'c'?"

requirement.description: The __getattr__ method in View class has incorrect error handling for reserved field names. It doesn't properly raise the expected AttributeError for reserved names accessed via attribute access.
requirement.contract: When accessing a reserved field name (starting with underscore) via attribute access, it should raise AttributeError with the specific message format: "View of (sig $signal) field '_c' has a reserved name and may only be accessed by indexing"

requirement.description: The __getitem__ method in View class has incorrect error handling for missing fields. It raises KeyError instead of AttributeError with the proper message format.
requirement.contract: When indexing with a missing field name, it should raise AttributeError with the proper message format instead of KeyError, and the message should include field name suggestions.
